entities.name: value type of a map type

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.condition: an element of an uninitialized map value, field or omitted field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of an uninitialized or omitted map value or field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be recursively expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element.
requirements.original: When referencing an element of an uninitialized map value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left-hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element as follows:

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: When a value or value field of map type is expanded, the element referenced by the index notation SHALL be set to present.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of map type, the element referenced by the index notation shall be set to present.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: During expansion of a map reference, expansion of record, record of, set of, union and set values and intermediate fields SHALL follow item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.3.0, 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.2.1 respectively.
requirements.original: b) Expansion of record, record of and set of, union and set values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.3.0 and 6.2.5.1 and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.
requirements.original: c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:map-value-type
requirements.canonical: A map type MAY have a nested structured type as its value (`to`) type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of map types with nested structured types for the to part.

requirements.subject: ent:map-value-type
requirements.canonical: The value (`to`) type of a map type MAY be a record, set, enumerated, set of, record of, union or map type.
requirements.original: The usage of structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of, record` `of, union and map) is allowed.`

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the permission of structured types applies only to the 'to' part (as the preceding sentence says) or also to the key type (the NOTE implies structured keys are allowed but discouraged). The 'to'-only reading is used here.
readings: The value (to) type of a map type MAY be a structured type.
Both the key (from) type and the value (to) type of a map type MAY be structured types.

requirements.subject: ent:map-key-type
requirements.canonical: The key type of a map type SHOULD be a basic type.
requirements.original: NOTE: It is recommended that only basic types are used for the keys of map types.

requirements.subject: ent:map-key-type
requirements.canonical: Using complex structured types as key type of a map type CAN have a negative impact on the speed of execution.
requirements.original: Using complex structured types for keys of map types can have negative impact on the speed of the execution.

requirements.subject: ent:map-value
requirements.canonical: In a map value, each key and its associated value field IS mandatory.
requirements.original: In map values, both keys and value fields associated with them are mandatory.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-symbol
requirements.canonical: The `omit` symbol SHALL NOT be assigned to a map key or to a map value field.
requirements.original: The omit symbol shall not be assigned to a map key or value field.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-statement
requirements.canonical: A key IS removed from a map by the `unmap` operation (not by assigning `omit`).
requirements.original: NOTE: The unmap operation is used for removing a key from a map.

ambiguity.issue: The NOTE calls it 'unmap operation' while clause 6.2.15.3 calls it 'unmap statement'; 'unmap operation' also denotes the port unmap operation.

requirements.subject: ent:map-key
requirements.canonical: A key of a map template SHALL NOT contain matching symbols.
requirements.original: Keys of map templates shall not contain matching symbols.

requirements.subject: ent:map-template
requirements.canonical: A value field associated with a key of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, including `omit`, `*` and `ifpresent`.
requirements.original: Value fields associated with keys of map templates might contain matching symbols including symbols for optional fields such as omit, * or ifpresent (see Annex B for more details).

ambiguity.issue: 6.2.15.9-s002 forbids assigning omit to a map value field, while this sentence allows omit, * and ifpresent in map template value fields; also 'might' can be read as permission or as possibility. The permission reading for templates is used.
readings: A value field of a map template MAY contain omit, * or ifpresent.
A value field of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, but omit (and therefore * / ifpresent with omit semantics) is excluded by the prohibition of omit for map value fields.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type IS represented by the keyword `any`.
requirements.original: The open type is represented by the keyword any.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL only be used as the type of a formal parameter of a predefined or external function.
requirements.original: a) The open type shall be used only in formal parameter of predefined or external functions.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: A value of any type MAY be passed directly as an actual parameter to a formal parameter of the open type without explicitly specifying a type context.
requirements.original: Values of all types can be directly passed as actual parameters to formal parameters of the open type without the need to explicitly specify a type context.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a type declaration.
requirements.original: Type declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a variable declaration.
requirements.original: Variable declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a template declaration.
requirements.original: Template declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a constant declaration.
requirements.original: Constant declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a module parameter declaration.
requirements.original: Module parameter declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in the return clause of a function.
requirements.original: Return clauses of functions

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used as the type of a formal parameter of a template, testcase, altstep, non-external function, map operation or unmap operation.
requirements.original: Formal parameters of templates, test cases, altsteps, non-external functions, map and unmap operations

ambiguity.issue: 'map and unmap operations' may denote the port map/unmap operations (which have a param clause) or the map type unmap statement of clause 6.2.15.3. The port operation reading is used.
readings: The open type SHALL NOT be used in the param clause of the port map and unmap operations.
The open type SHALL NOT be used as an argument type of the unmap statement on map variables (clause 6.2.15.3).

non_requirement.reason: NOTE introducing the list of forbidden contexts; each listed context is extracted from 6.2.16-s006..s012.
